sections.h2: Which Sullivan County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, and neither sets the rate. The Property Assessor, Donna Whitaker, values every parcel from 3411 Highway 126, Suite 103, in Blountville (423-323-6455, staffed on weekdays from eight to five). The Trustee collects the money at 1651 Blountville Boulevard, Suite 104, Blountville, TN 37617 (423-323-6464, with the same Monday to Friday schedule). The County Commission picks the rate each year.

The Trustee also keeps two seasonal counters, in Bristol at 801 Anderson Street, Room 139 (Thursday and Friday) and in Kingsport at 225 West Center Street, #101 (Monday through Wednesday). Both run only from October 1 to March 15, close from 1:30 to 2:30 p.m. for lunch and shut on holidays and election days.

Inside Bristol, Kingsport or Bluff City, a house may also receive a city bill, as the Trustee's FAQ explains. Ask the city about its own rate and due date.

sections.h2: How does Blountville's county compare in size and housing?
sections.html:
Sullivan County fills the northeast corner of Tennessee along the Virginia line. It was cut from Washington County in 1779 and covers 430 square miles, of which 413 are land. Kingsport has the most residents, and Bristol, Bluff City and a slice of Johnson City also fall inside. Blountville, the county seat, is the only unincorporated county seat in Tennessee.

The land runs from Ridge-and-Valley ridges in the west to the Blue Ridge in the east, where Holston Mountain tops out at 4,284 feet. Kingsport is where the North and South Forks of the Holston River meet. The county splits into three school systems: Bristol Tennessee City Schools, Kingsport City School District and Sullivan County Schools, so a buyer's zone depends on the address.

Census Bureau QuickFacts show a lower price level than nearby Sumner County:

  • 163,759 residents in July 2025, up 3.5% from April 2020
  • 77,633 housing units, 72.1% occupied by their owners
  • Typical home value of $213,300 among owner-occupied units, per the 2020 to 2024 survey
  • Rent around $889 a month and household income around $58,807, both medians
  • 771 building permits in 2025

sections.h2: How is a Sullivan County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ explains the math: take 25 percent of the property's value, then multiply by the county rate. The 2025 county rate shown there is $1.6129 for every $100 of assessed value. On a $250,000 house, the assessed value is $62,500, so the year's county tax comes to about $1,008.

Each bill covers one calendar year. Business furniture and equipment are taxed too, and owners must file a personal property schedule each year. The Assessor adds that the next county-wide reappraisal is set for 2027, so values can change again before long.

sections.h2: When does Sullivan County want its tax, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
Payment opens when the bill falls due in early October, and it stays penalty free until the end of February. The Trustee lists no discount for paying early. On March 1 the balance turns delinquent and 1.5 percent interest is added each month.

Ways to pay include:

  • In person in Blountville, Bristol or Kingsport
  • By mail to PO Box 550, Blountville, TN 37617, or the Blountville drop box
  • Online or by phone, with a card fee of 2.5 percent or an e-check fee of $1.25, both kept by the processor
  • At Bank of Tennessee branches with the notice, cash or check only

Installments are allowed between October 1 and February 28, though the owner must track the balance. No notice is required by law, so a bill that never arrives still accrues interest.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Sullivan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a call to the Assessor's office, then take the dispute to the county equalization board, which the state schedule has meeting June 1. Taking it to the state board must happen by August 1, or 45 days from the local board's mailed notice, if that comes later. For tax year 2026 the August date has passed, so an owner holding a later notice should call 615-401-7883 to check the 45-day window.

The state's guidance says the best proof for a house is sales of comparable homes, with differences in size, age, condition and location explained. An appraisal may also be offered. A statement that a house is overvalued, with no figure behind it, is usually not enough. The taxpayer must still pay the undisputed part of the bill on time, along with any older delinquent tax.

sections.h2: What tax relief is there for Sullivan County homeowners?
sections.html:
The state relief rebate covers owners who live in their home and are 65 or older, disabled, or a qualifying disabled veteran or widow of one. Elderly and disabled applicants may have combined household income of no more than $38,470, spouse included. Bring proof of income, a Social Security card and proof of residency and age. Call 423-323-6470 or 423-323-6469 for an appointment.

The signed voucher must come back to a Trustee office each year by April 5, and bank branches do not accept it. Sullivan County does not offer a tax freeze program.

sections.h2: Can a Sullivan County owner qualify for greenbelt or an exemption?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office also manages Greenbelt and Forestry assessments. The state calendar sets March 15 as the greenbelt application deadline and May 20 for exemption applications. An owner of acreage should call the Assessor about both programs before listing.

Anyone who owns a business furnishing or equipment on January 1 may owe personal property tax even after closing the shop. The Trustee says the business must be formally closed with the right agencies.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Sullivan County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever held title on January 1 gets the notice, even when the house changes hands later in the year. The Trustee says new owners still must see that the tax is paid on time, and to follow the settlement statement for the split. If a lender escrows the taxes, the mortgage company gets the bill.

A seller with unpaid tax should settle the balance with the Trustee before closing. Interest can be removed only by a court order or an assessment change from the State Board or the Assessor, so a late bill rarely gets waived.

faqs.q: What is the Sullivan County property tax rate?
faqs.a: For 2025 the Trustee shows a county levy of $1.6129 for each $100 assessed. Homes are assessed at 25 percent of value, and cities may add their own tax.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Sullivan County taxes early?
faqs.a: No discount is listed. Taxes can be paid without penalty from October 1 through February 28, and the Trustee permits installments in that window.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Sullivan County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Trustee in Blountville, or at the seasonal Bristol and Kingsport counters from October 1 through March 15. Bank of Tennessee branches also take cash or check payments with the notice.

faqs.q: Does Sullivan County offer a property tax freeze?
faqs.a: No. The Trustee says Sullivan County does not currently offer a freeze program, though the state tax relief rebate is available to qualifying seniors, disabled owners and veterans.

faqs.q: When is the next Sullivan County reappraisal?
faqs.a: The Assessor's page lists 2027 as the next county-wide reappraisal. The Assessor's 2025 update described a reappraisal that year, with revaluation notices going out in the spring.
